claims.text: HCM: a beta-blocker or a non-DHP (diltiazem, verapamil) is first-line;
claims.quote: First-line pharmacologic therapy consists of beta-blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, verapamil) (1).

claims.text: they slow the HR, lengthen diastolic filling and lessen LVOT obstruction.
claims.quote: These medications decrease heart rate and prolong the diastolic filling interval, thereby augmenting preload, and attenuate LVOT obstruction through their negative inotropic effects.

claims.text: Avoid verapamil with severe dyspnea at rest, hypotension, an LVOT gradient ≥ 100 mm Hg, and in children.
claims.quote: Verapamil should be avoided in patients with severe dyspnea at rest, hypotension, or a LVOT gradient ≥ 100 mm Hg and in children

claims.text: CCBs should generally be stopped if persistent LV systolic dysfunction develops.
claims.quote: Therapies with negative inotropic effects, including calcium channel blockers, and cardiac myosin inhibitors, should generally be discontinued and guideline-directed medical therapy should be instituted in patients with persistent LV systolic dysfunction.

claims.text: Overdose: DHPs cause marked hypotension, possibly with reflex tachycardia;

claims.text: non-DHPs cause bradycardia, hypotension and heart block.
